evidence: 0090 (D17, owner decisions D17-1 to D17-13 of 2026-10-26, every recommended default) lets the receiving laboratory or pharmacy withdraw what it recorded on an order it accepted for someone who was not the order's patient after that order has ended or its window has lapsed, until 180 days after it accepted the order; item 3's report (0088's ehr.report_wrong_patient_order_route) is unchanged byte for byte. ehr.correct_wrong_patient_order_route (owner-only), through lab.correct_wrong_patient_order_route and pharmacy.correct_wrong_patient_order_route, is bound to the live direct-care staff session and the kind's receive permission; in one READ COMMITTED transaction it repeats item 3's withdrawal statement for statement (every result marked entered in error and every version the ordering facility holds reported withdrawn there, or the dispensing reversed; lab.result.entered-in-error or pharmacy.dispensing.reverse when something must be withdrawn), ends a lapsed route through 0086's closer (ended_kind 'wrong_patient') and keeps the ending of a route that had ended, and writes the report row (late, ended_kind_before, discovered_by, discovered_on), a system row at each facility and the patient's notice (ORDER_ROUTE_WRONG_PATIENT_CORRECTED for an order that had ended). At most 5 late corrections per member and 20 per facility in any 24 hours, exact under a transaction advisory lock per receiving facility (ORDER_ROUTE_CORRECTION_LIMIT, DETAIL the time another is possible; measured with two concurrent sessions at 19 and at 4). B's access to the patient is never reopened: the command writes one row of the new ehr.order_route_correction_capabilities (forced row-level security, no grant to any role), keyed by pg_current_xact_id(), which H6 (ehr.order_route_access_allows, md5 20d9847baf91a6b801ff1db2127ce2a7, replaced with 0086's body plus one branch inside its no-route test) honours only inside that transaction (pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned(), never txid_current(), so a read-only transaction pays one function call), only for that facility, patient, kind and member, and still behind the control and the receive permission; the command deletes it before it returns (measured after every committed correction of the concurrency runs: the table empty, its inserts equal to its deletes plus the transactions rolled back after writing it). B's lookup ehr.find_correctable_order_routes, through lab.find_correctable_order_routes and pharmacy.find_correctable_order_routes, finds an accepted order by its exact reference (at most 5, the char(8) index) with its correction state and, only while open or correctable, B's own facts about it, never a patient, orderer, work item or value. Item access (md5 fc1316081592f96211c6163e72212703) and the release trigger lab.return_order_route_result (md5 16b4808a4813b4e4449442ef19f4540d) treat a route with a report as ended wrong_patient (a release is refused, 23514 ORDER_ROUTE_CLOSED). The ordering facility's summary gains wrongPatient and correctableUntil computed inline; its Overview read (C28) is keyed on the report; the patient's list (C5), support's reports list (C26: the late columns, the reporter's late count, whether the sender is still active, the required actions and three flags) and support's find (C21: the correction state and deadline, each helper once per returned row) are dropped and created with trailing columns, given back to their recorded owners with their attributes checked and their grants compared as sets with those recorded before the drop; support's review (C27) refuses a late report without the actions it requires (22023 WRONG_PATIENT_REVIEW_REFERRAL_REQUIRED, DETAIL the missing ones), as the report table's new CHECK does; its guard keeps the four new columns fixed. Preconditions pin the ten replaced or dropped bodies and 49 relied-upon bodies (md5 of pg_proc.prosrc measured on 0001-0089), the report table's CHECKs, keys and columns and the route and event CHECKs relied upon (compared with the same objects built in the session), the triggers and xid8, and require one owner (H6's) that holds every privilege the new bodies need, and every role that runs a body reading the report table to read it, counted by ownership, membership or grant and never through a superuser's bypass (79 refusing cases measured, each stopping in the preconditions with nothing applied, among them a copy with 0087-0089 applied as another role). Locks (pg_locks at every section boundary, dry run and apply, as the migrator and as a NOSUPERUSER owner): momentary ACCESS SHARE on ehr.order_routes, ehr.order_route_events and the report table (pg_get_constraintdef) and on lab.result_revisions (the PL/pgSQL validator), each released at once; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the report table alone, NOWAIT, 50 attempts over 5 seconds, then 55P03 with nothing applied (measured with a reader holding ACCESS SHARE, in the dry run and in the apply), held to commit for 27-41 ms on a small copy and with 100,000 routes; ACCESS SHARE on identity.facilities and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the new table to commit; with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE held on any of those five tables the runner's lock_timeout stops the release after 5 seconds with nothing applied; nothing on platform.control_settings, identity.consent_grants or any other chain table. Old images on the new schema: bd8676e's and 3610a4a's Identity, EHR, Lab and Pharmacy pass their order-routes runtime verifier end to end on a 0090 copy once its exact comparison of support's flags ignores the new patient_reported_before (the only change to either verifier); 3610a4a's database suites pass unchanged on 0090 apart from the four checks that name C21's 15 columns, the function and grant counts, the Overview row's exact keys and support's exact flags; the old Identity answers a review the new rule refuses 400 WRONG_PATIENT_REVIEW_INVALID, and only the new services write late reports. Grants: the four Lab and Pharmacy wrappers to their runtimes and hid_schema_test_runtime, C5 again to hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, C21 and C26 again to hid_identity_runtime alone, in the migration and in runtime-grants.sql; the new table, the two helpers and the shared command and lookup to no role. Suites: services/ehr-api/test/database/order-routes-late-correction.integration.sql, with the order-routes privileges, contract-fields, wrong-patient, wrong-patient-overview, patient, returns, lifecycle and concurrency suites and the Lab session guards extended.
